title: Flood: turn around, don't drown
body: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood water. Six inches of moving water can knock a person down; one foot can sweep a vehicle away. Move to higher ground. Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.

title: Household evacuation plan
body: Leave immediately if you are in danger. Otherwise leave when local officials issue an evacuation order. Primary meeting point: Demo Community Center parking lot. Backup: Demo Library. Take the go-bag, medications and pet carrier. Text one out-of-area contact instead of calling.

title: Go-bag checklist
body: Water (1 gallon per person per day, 3 days), non-perishable food, flashlight, extra batteries, first aid kit, copies of ID and insurance, phone charger and power bank, cash, whistle, 7-day supply of medications, local paper map.

title: Power outage and carbon monoxide
body: Never run a generator, grill or camp stove indoors or in a garage, even with the door open: carbon monoxide can kill. Keep freezer and fridge closed (fridge stays cold about 4 hours, full freezer about 48 hours). Unplug electronics to avoid surge damage when power returns.

title: Household medications
body: Resident A takes a daily prescription that must stay refrigerated. Storage limits outside the fridge are on the pharmacy label; check the label or ask a pharmacist. Keep a printed medication list in the go-bag.

title: Earthquake and gas leaks
body: During shaking: drop, cover and hold on; stay indoors until shaking stops. Afterward, check for injuries and gas leaks. If you smell gas, leave the building and do not use switches or flames. Expect aftershocks.
